title: I Took the Self-Storage Access Hours to the Manager Who Let His Truck In

parts.text: Gate hours ended at 9:00 p.m. and at 9:11 the manager's pickup was inside with my unit hallway lights on. The keypad card said: ACCESS 6–9. MANAGER AFTER 9 FOR ALARMS ONLY. I was forty-one, tenant, holding a denied pin. Manager Cole waved from the truck. "Trucks are alarms." I photographed the time, the card, and the pickup at my hallway. Then I logged an after-hours. At 9:18 regional asked why Cole's truck was on a 9:11 still. I waited where the camera already was. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Regional can see the manager's pickup inside after 9 against the keypad card.

social.video_title: The manager drove a pickup in after access hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Self-storage, a denied pin, and a truck in the hall. I logged after-hours. Would you have photographed the time?

parts.text: Cole called it a check until regional asked for the log. I printed the after-hours, the photo, and the card. The truck left. Cole checked alarms on foot and told tenants checks were always about optics. Optics is a word managers use when a pickup exists. Access now has a second line: TRUCKS ARE NOT ALARMS. I keep 6–9. Cole walks. The gate finally looks like hours, not a driveway. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: After-hours log, empty hall, and a second line. Was a check ever a pickup?
